input.prompt:
Build a small coordination CLI called `hq` for a hackathon repo where 2 humans each run several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) coordinated through GitHub Issues. Work in /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/cayenne. Be fast; a teammate is waiting.

CREATE ONLY THESE FILES (other people are editing other files in this same directory right now; do not touch anything else, do not run `git add/commit/push/switch`, and do not run any `gh` command that writes to GitHub — read-only gh like `gh pr list --json` with no fields, to see available fields, is fine; the GitHub repo ehewes/durhack-proj currently has no issues/PRs and its remote is empty):
- `hq` (POSIX sh shim, chmod +x): `#!/bin/sh` then `exec python3 "$(dirname "$0")/tools/hq/hq.py" "$@"`
- `hq.cmd` (Windows shim): `@python "%~dp0tools\hq\hq.py" %*`
- `hq.json`: `{"default_branch": "main", "lanes": {}, "check": [], "setup": [], "stale_minutes": 60}` (lanes format: `{"<lane>": {"owner": "<github login>", "paths": ["dir/"]}}`)
- `tools/hq/hq.py` (python3 stdlib only, MUST run on Python 3.9: no `match`, no PEP 604 unions at runtime, `from __future__ import annotations` is fine; argparse subcommands)
- `tools/hq/tests/test_hq.py` (unittest; import hq.py via importlib from its path). TDD: write tests for the pure logic first, then implement. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/hq/tests -v` until green.

Design: pure functions (parsing/decisions, unit-tested, take plain dicts/lists) separated from I/O (`gh`/`git` via subprocess, JSON output). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 refused by a gate, 3 lost a claim race. Output plain and short (agents read it); symbols ✓ ✗ ! allowed. Repo root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; config read from `<root>/hq.json`. owner/repo from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.

Issue body format (GitHub issue forms render each field as `### <label>` then the value; empty optional fields render as `_No response_`, treat that as empty). Headings: `### Goal`, `### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`, `### Notes`. `Blocked by` contains refs like `#12, #14` or `none`. `Scope` contains paths/globs (e.g. `web/src/`, `api/*.py`), one per line or comma separated, possibly in backticks or as `- ` bullets.

Identity: login = `gh api user --jq .login` (cache per process); agent = `--agent` or env HQ_AGENT (default `agent`); workspace = `--workspace` or env CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME or basename of the worktree root. id = `<login>/<agent>/<workspace>`.

Claim protocol (race-safe without a lock; two humans): claim comment body starts with `<!-- hq:claim id=<id> branch=<branch> -->` then a line like `Claimed by **<login>** via `<agent>` (workspace `<ws>`) on branch `<branch>``. Release comment starts with `<!-- hq:release id=<id> -->` + optional note. Active claims = claim markers with no LATER release marker for the same id (comment order / createdAt). Winner = earliest active claim (createdAt, tie -> list order).

Commands:
1. `setup [--check | --ci]`. Checklist with ✓/✗/! (warning) and a fix hint per item: python>=3.9; `gh` installed and `gh auth status` ok; `gh repo view` works; `git config user.email` set; `entire --version` works (! if missing, hint: brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire); `<root>/.entire/settings.json` has `checkpoints.primary.type == "git-branch"` (! otherwise, hint `entire configure --checkpoint-backend branch`); guard installed: `<git-common-dir>/hooks/pre-commit` contains marker `hq-guard`; `git config --get gc.auto` == `0`; if env CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH is set, `$CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH/.codex/hooks.json` exists (! hint: `git -C "$CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH" pull --ff-only` so Codex finds its hooks); ! if current branch is the default branch. Default mode (no flag) FIXES what it can, then prints the checklist: install guard shim into the shared hooks dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` + `/hooks/pre-commit`): if absent write
   ```
   #!/bin/sh
   # hq-guard: run the versioned guard
   root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
   if [ -x "$root/.githooks/pre-commit" ]; then "$root/.githooks/pre-commit" "$@" || exit $?; fi
   [ -x "$(dirname "$0")/pre-commit.local" ] && exec "$(dirname "$0")/pre-commit.local" "$@"
   exit 0
   ```
   and chmod +x; if a pre-commit exists WITHOUT the marker, move it to `pre-commit.local` first (keeps chaining). Set `git config gc.auto 0`. Run each `hq.json` `setup` command (shell=True) and report. `--check` only reports (exit 1 if any ✗; warnings don't fail). `--ci` only runs `hq.json` setup commands (no gh/git checks).
2. `bootstrap` (idempotent, run once per repo): labels via `gh label create NAME --color HEX --description D --force`: status:ready(0e8a16) status:in-progress(fbca04) status:review(1d76db) status:blocked(b60205) status:needs-human(5319e7) P0(b60205,"Demo-critical") P1(d93f0b) P2(c2e0c6) size:S(c5def5,"<=30 min of agent time") size:M(bfd4f2,"<=90 min") size:L(5319e7,"Too big: split it") type:feat type:bug type:chore type:spike type:docs review:pass(0e8a16) review:changes(d93f0b) agent:claude agent:codex agent:cursor epic, plus `lane:<name>` for each hq.json lane. Milestones (create missing via `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/milestones`): "M0 Skeleton", "M1 MVP demo path", "M2 Prizes + polish", "M3 Submission". Repo settings: `gh api -X PATCH repos/{o}/{r} -F allow_squash_merge=true -F allow_merge_commit=false -F allow_rebase_merge=false -F delete_branch_on_merge=true -f squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE -f squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES` (keeps Entire-Checkpoint trailers in squash commits). Ruleset: if none named `hq-protect-main` exists (`gh api repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets`), POST JSON via `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets --input -`: name hq-protect-main, target branch, enforcement active, conditions.ref_name.include ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"] exclude [], rules: deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request with parameters {required_approving_review_count:0, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push:false, require_code_owner_review:false, require_last_push_approval:false, required_review_thread_resolution:false}. If GitHub refuses (403/422, e.g. private repo without Pro), print `! ruleset unavailable: <reason>; the pre-commit guard is the protection` and continue. Print a summary.
3. `board [--brief]`: data from `gh issue list --state open --limit 200 --json number,title,labels,assignees,updatedAt,body` and `gh pr list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,headRefName,isDraft,labels,statusCheckRollup,mergeable,updatedAt,files,closingIssuesReferences` (verify `files` is a valid list field; if not, fetch files per PR with `gh pr view N --json files`). For in-progress issues, get the active claim id from comments (`gh issue view N --json comments`; skip this in --brief). Sections: IN PROGRESS (#, title, claimer id or assignee, age, linked PR), REVIEW (PR #, issue, CI ✓/✗/…, review:pass/changes, draft, CONFLICTING), NEEDS HUMAN, BLOCKED (with open blockers), READY (sorted lane, then P0<P1<P2<none, then S<M<L), OVERLAPS (files touched by more than one open PR, with PR numbers), STALE (in-progress with updatedAt older than stale_minutes). `--brief`: at most ~15 lines (counts, in-progress list, overlaps, top 5 ready).
4. `claim N --agent A [--workspace W]`: fetch `gh issue view N --json number,title,body,state,labels,assignees,comments,url`. Refuse (exit 2) if not OPEN; if any `Blocked by` ref is still OPEN (check each with `gh issue view R --json state`); if another id holds an active claim (say who and since when). If my id already holds it, say so and continue (idempotent). If current branch is the default branch or detached, `git switch -c <login>/<N>-<slug>` (slug: lowercase alnum and hyphens from title, max 40 chars). Post claim comment (`gh issue comment N --body-file -`), re-fetch comments; if the winner is not me, post my release marker with note `lost race to <winner>` and exit 3. Then `gh issue edit N --add-assignee @me --add-label status:in-progress --remove-label status:ready` and add `agent:<A>` only when A is claude/codex/cursor (if edit fails because a label is missing, retry without the remove/agent label and warn). Print: title + url, the issue body, IN FLIGHT (other in-progress issues: # title assignees) and OVERLAPS between this issue's Scope paths and files in open PRs (prefix or fnmatch match), then a short NEXT STEPS reminder: context via `entire search`/`entire graph query`/`entire brain brief`, small commits staging files by name, `./hq check`, `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`.
5. `release N [--needs-human] [--note TEXT] [--agent A] [--workspace W]`: post release marker (+ note). Labels: remove status:in-progress, add status:needs-human if flag else status:ready. Remove assignee @me only if no other active claim by my login remains.
6. `pr N --body-file F [--draft] [--agent A] [--allow-dirty] [--no-rebase-check]`: refuse on default branch; refuse if `git status --porcelain` is non-empty (unless --allow-dirty); `git fetch origin <default>` and, if `origin/<default>` exists and is not an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), refuse with `rebase first: git rebase origin/<default>, then ./hq check` (unless --no-rebase-check); `git push -u origin HEAD`. Title `<issue title> (#N)`; body = file contents + `\n\nCloses #N\n\n---\nAgent: `<id>``. If an open PR for this head branch exists (`gh pr list --head <branch> --state open --json number,url`), `gh pr edit` title/body; else `gh pr create --base <default> --head <branch> --title ... --body-file -` (+ --draft). Copy issue labels matching `lane:*`, `P0/P1/P2`, `agent:*`, `size:*`, `type:*` onto the PR. Issue: add status:review, remove status:in-progress. Print the PR URL and NEXT STEPS: `entire trail create --title "<title> (#N)" --type feature`, `entire trail ci-pr`, `entire review` unless size:S, then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
7. `ship PR [--skip-review]`: `gh pr view PR --json number,title,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,labels,statusCheckRollup,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,url`; if mergeable is UNKNOWN retry up to 3x with a 2s sleep. Gates (print each failing gate, exit 2): state OPEN, not draft, not CONFLICTING, checks: every CheckRun has status COMPLETED with conclusion SUCCESS/NEUTRAL/SKIPPED and every StatusContext has state SUCCESS (pending -> refuse "checks still running"; zero checks is OK), label review:pass present unless --skip-review. Merge with `gh pr merge PR --squash` (NO --delete-branch: it breaks inside worktrees; the repo setting deletes the remote branch). Then unblock: for open issues labelled status:blocked, parse `Blocked by`; if all refs are now closed, add status:ready, remove status:blocked, comment `Unblocked: #X merged in #PR`. Print merged PR and the unblocked issues.
8. `check`: run each `hq.json` `check` command (shell=True, capture output); print `✓ <cmd> (1.2s)` or `✗ <cmd> (exit N)` followed by the last 30 lines of its output; run all; exit 1 if any failed. If none configured print `no checks configured yet (hq.json "check")` and exit 0.

Unit-test at least: section parsing incl. `_No response_` and `none`, issue-ref parsing, scope-path parsing, active-claim computation (release later/earlier, two ids, ties), winner selection, slugify, overlap map, scope-vs-file matching, stale detection, check-rollup evaluation (success/pending/failure/StatusContext/empty), ship gate evaluation, ready-queue sorting.

When done, also run `./hq --help`, `./hq check`, and `./hq setup --check` (read-only) and include their output (trimmed) in your report. Report: files created, test count/result, any deviation from this spec and why. Keep the report under 300 words.

Issue body headings (the issue form labels MUST be exactly these so GitHub renders `### <label>` headings that hq parses): Goal, Acceptance criteria, Scope (files/dirs this issue may touch), Do not touch, Blocked by (`#12, #14` or `none`), Verify (commands or manual steps), Notes. In task.yml make Goal and Acceptance criteria required, default label `status:ready`.

AGENTS.md must cover, tersely:
1. Context lives in `docs/hack/BRIEF.md` (event, prizes, deadlines), `docs/SPEC.md` (what we build, demo path), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (stack, lanes, contracts), `docs/DECISIONS.md`. Read only what your issue needs.

Full detail: `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`.
3. Git rules: work only in your own worktree and branch; never commit on main (a hook blocks it); stage files by name (never `git add -A` or `.`); never revert, checkout, stash or delete changes you did not make; never amend or force-push pushed commits; rebase on `origin/main` before `./hq pr` and fix your own conflicts. 6. Issues are approved designs: do not run brainstorming, spec or plan-document rituals for issue work; plan inline and build.
7. Entire records every session and pushes transcripts with your commits: never paste secrets, tokens or .env contents into prompts or code. Do not disable Entire.

Skills are in `.claude/skills` (`/hq-work`, `/hq-plan`, `/hq-review`, `/hq-ship`).

Skills:
- hq-work: the full loop with exact commands, a PR body template (What changed / How verified with the `./hq check` tail / Risks / Screenshots), conflict handling (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, re-run check), out-of-scope and stuck handling, the definition of done.

Rules: 1 issue = 1 agent = 1 PR, size S or M (L must be split), parallel issues must have disjoint Scope paths, contracts and skeleton first in M0 (shared types, API stubs, CI check commands, deploy) with everything else `Blocked by` them, P0 = on the demo path. input.description: Read the rest of the house commit style

result.output:
```
<Imperative subject: what the product or system gained>

<Paragraph: what exists now, and honestly what it still does not do.>

<Optional second paragraph: the one decision worth defending, and why.>

- Filename.php: what changed here and why.
- area or filename: what changed here and why.
- tests: what is covered, and how the assertions were proven to have teeth.
```

## The subject line

Imperative, no full stop, names what was added or changed at product level.

Good, taken from real commits in this style:

```
Add the relational policy schema, models and the attention rule
Import legacy governance into relational policies and add the library index
Gate every governance write on canEditWorkspace
Scope policies to the property group
Align policies-v2 docs to company ownership
```

If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## The opening paragraph: be additive

This is the part that goes wrong. Lead with **what the system can now do**, and
state plainly what it still cannot. Two real examples:

> First structural phase of the Policies rebuild: the tables exist and are
> unit-testable, and nothing reads them yet, so the change is additive and
> invisible.

> The importer builds each workspace from the real taxonomy and only overlays
> whatever was saved before, because the old data can't be trusted.

Both open with the thing that now exists. Neither opens with the process of
building it.

## Bullets

One per file or area. **Bare filenames or short area names, never full paths.**
Dense prose sentences, not fragments. Reasoning inline, in the same sentence as
the change.

```
- PolicyEventTypeEnum.php: fourteen cases, the single vocabulary behind history
  chips, the Agent Log filter options and the WorkOS action names. Values stay
  inside string(32) so the column does not need widening.
- migrations: policy_events gains uuid, correlation_id and mirrored_at. uuid is
  the event's public identity and the WorkOS idempotency key, so a retried mirror
  cannot duplicate upstream.
```

Group related files under one area bullet (`migrations:`, `tests:`) rather than
listing each.

The last bullet is always `tests:`, covering what is asserted and, where
mutation testing was done, that the assertions fail without the fix.

## Plain words, and few of them

Write for someone skimming `git log`, not for someone admiring the design.

**Cut invented precision.** Phrases that sound exact but carry no meaning to a
reader: "taxonomy positions", "the canonical vocabulary", "the seam", "first-class
records", "the discipline". If a plainer sentence says the same thing, use it.

    no    References are taxonomy positions, not free text
    yes   A new policy is numbered automatically from its category

    no    the write path funnels through a single mutation surface
    yes   all edits go through PolicyWriteService

**Keep bullets to one or two sentences.** If a bullet needs three, either the
change is doing too much or the detail belongs in the code comment instead.

**Say the effect, not the mechanism**, unless the mechanism is the point.

    no    ds-form-control applies text-transform uppercase and the console body
          carries the hq-app class so the cascade reaches it
    yes   dialog fields show what was typed. They were inheriting the HQ form
          style, which forces uppercase.

**Target length.** Subject, a short paragraph, one optional second paragraph, then
one bullet per file. If it runs much past that, cut rather than reorganise.

## Do not

- **Tell the story of finding the bug.** "Two faults surfaced only by driving it",
  "a test caught", "it turned out", "I discovered". The reader wants the state of
  the system, not the diary. If a fault is worth mentioning, say what the code now
  does and why, in one clause.
- **Lead with process.** Not "after the merge I ran the suite and". Lead with the change.
- **Headline test counts.** "195 tests passing" belongs in chat, not the message.
  Numbers that age badly do not belong in permanent history.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/.claude/skills/commit-message

# Commit messages, house style

Read this before drafting. The failure mode is drifting into an engineering
narrative, and it is easy to do without noticing.

## The flow: draft, confirm, commit, they push

1. **Draft** the message and show it in one plain code block.
2. **Wait.** Never commit on the same turn as the draft. The user is reviewing both
   the message and the commit boundary.
3. **On confirmation**, write the body to `.context/commit-message.txt` (gitignored),
   `git add` only that stage's files, then
   `git commit -F .context/commit-message.txt`.
4. **Stop.** Never `git push`. The user pushes once they agree with what landed.

### Authorship, non-negotiable

The commit is the user's. Their git config supplies the author. Never pass `--author`,
never add `Co-Authored-By`, never add any AI attribution or trailer line of any kind.

### Before committing, mechanically check

    python3 -c "import sys;b=open('.context/commit-message.txt',encoding='utf-8').read();\
    bad=[c for c in b if c in '\u2014\u2013'];print('DASHES:',bad or 'none')"

Any hit, rewrite it. Colons, commas or hyphens instead. Also confirm no `Co-Authored-By`,
no full file paths, and no test counts in the body.

### Scope

One stage per commit. Add that stage's files by name rather than `git add -A`, unless the
user says otherwise. If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## Shape

```
<Imperative subject: what the product or system gained>

<Paragraph: what exists now, and honestly what it still does not do.>

<Optional second paragraph: the one decision worth defending, and why.>

- Filename.php: what changed here and why.
- area or filename: what changed here and why.
- tests: what is covered, and how the assertions were proven to have teeth.
```

## The subject line

Imperative, no full stop, names what was added or changed at product level.

Good, taken from real commits in this style:

```
Add the relational policy schema, models and the attention rule
Import legacy governance into relational policies and add the library index
Gate every governance write on canEditWorkspace
Scope policies to the property group
Align policies-v2 docs to company ownership
```

If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## The opening paragraph: be additive

This is the part that goes wrong. Lead with **what the system can now do**, and
state plainly what it still cannot. Two real examples:

> First structural phase of the Policies rebuild: the tables exist and are
> unit-testable, and nothing reads them yet, so the change is additive and
> invisible.

> The importer builds each workspace from the real taxonomy and only overlays
> whatever was saved before, because the old data can't be trusted.

Both open with the thing that now exists. Neither opens with the process of
building it.

## Bullets

One per file or area. **Bare filenames or short area names, never full paths.**
Dense prose sentences, not fragments. Reasoning inline, in the same sentence as
the change.

```
- PolicyEventTypeEnum.php: fourteen cases, the single vocabulary behind history
  chips, the Agent Log filter options and the WorkOS action names. Values stay
  inside string(32) so the column does not need widening.
- migrations: policy_events gains uuid, correlation_id and mirrored_at. uuid is
  the event's public identity and the WorkOS idempotency key, so a retried mirror
  cannot duplicate upstream.
```

Group related files under one area bullet (`migrations:`, `tests:`) rather than
listing each.

The last bullet is always `tests:`, covering what is asserted and, where
mutation testing was done, that the assertions fail without the fix.

## Plain words, and few of them

Write for someone skimming `git log`, not for someone admiring the design.

**Cut invented precision.** Phrases that sound exact but carry no meaning to a
reader: "taxonomy positions", "the canonical vocabulary", "the seam", "first-class
records", "the discipline". If a plainer sentence says the same thing, use it.

    no    References are taxonomy positions, not free text
    yes   A new policy is numbered automatically from its category

    no    the write path funnels through a single mutation surface
    yes   all edits go through PolicyWriteService

**Keep bullets to one or two sentences.** If a bullet needs three, either the
change is doing too much or the detail belongs in the code comment instead.

**Say the effect, not the mechanism**, unless the mechanism is the point.

    no    ds-form-control applies text-transform uppercase and the console body
          carries the hq-app class so the cascade reaches it
    yes   dialog fields show what was typed. They were inheriting the HQ form
          style, which forces uppercase.

**Target length.** Subject, a short paragraph, one optional second paragraph, then
one bullet per file. If it runs much past that, cut rather than reorganise.

## Do not

- **Tell the story of finding the bug.** "Two faults surfaced only by driving it",
  "a test caught", "it turned out", "I discovered". The reader wants the state of
  the system, not the diary. If a fault is worth mentioning, say what the code now
  does and why, in one clause.
- **Lead with process.** Not "after the merge I ran the suite and". Lead with the change.
- **Headline test counts.** "195 tests passing" belongs in chat, not the message.
  Numbers that age badly do not belong in permanent history.
- **Use full file paths.** `PolicyWriteService.php`, not
  `app/Services/Policies/PolicyWriteService.php`.
- **Use em-dashes anywhere.** Colons, commas or hyphens instead. This applies to
  every generated artifact, not just commits.
- **Narrate the plan.** No stage numbers, phase names, ticket references or
  "as agreed". The commit records the code, not the schedule.

## Self-check before handing it over

1. Does the first sentence say what the system can now do?
2. Could a reader who was not in the conversation follow it?
3. Is every bullet a change plus its reason, rather than a list of edits?
4. Any discovery narrative left? Cut it.
5. Any em-dash? Any full path? Any test count in the body? Cut them.
6. Would the subject still make sense in a changelog?

# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent in this repo: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Short on purpose.

## Context
- `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`: event, prizes, deadlines.
- `docs/SPEC.md`: what we build, the demo path.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: stack, lanes, contracts.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: decisions so far.

Read only what your issue needs.

## The loop
One issue = one agent = one worktree/branch = one PR. Humans assign issues. Never pick your own.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <claude|codex|cursor>`.
2. Context before code: `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"`,
   `entire brain brief "<task>"`. Run `entire why <file>:<line>` before rewriting code you did not write.
3. Build inside the issue's Scope, in small commits.
4. `./hq check` must pass.
5. Open the PR: `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`.
6. Trail: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`, then `entire trail ci-pr`.
7. Unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`, fix the findings,
   `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`, then `entire trail ready`.
8. Stop and report. Only when a human says "ship it": `./hq ship <PR>`.

Full detail: `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`. Also useful: `./hq board`, `./hq setup --check`.
Windows: use `hq.cmd` or `python tools/hq/hq.py` wherever this file says `./hq`.

## Git
- Work only in your own worktree and branch. Never commit on `main` (a hook blocks it).
- Stage files by name. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`.
- Never revert, checkout, stash or delete changes you did not make.
- Never amend or force-push commits that are already pushed.
- Before `./hq pr`, rebase on `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`) and fix
  your own conflicts. If your branch is already pushed, `git merge origin/main` instead.
- Commit and push your own branch freely. No need to ask.

## Coordination
- GitHub is the only shared state. `.context/` is your private scratch.
- Out-of-scope work becomes a new issue (`gh issue create`), not a drive-by edit.
- Never edit paths listed under "Do not touch" in your issue.
- Progress notes go in issue comments: `gh issue comment N --body "..."`.
- Stuck: `./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
- Contract changes (shared types, API shapes) need their own issue.

## Definition of done
- Every acceptance criterion is met.
- `./hq check` passes, with its tail in the PR body.
- The PR is open with evidence: what you ran and what you saw.
- Review passed (`review:pass`), unless the issue is `size:S`.

## Issues are approved designs
Do not run brainstorming, spec or plan-document rituals for issue work. Plan inline, then build.

## Entire
Entire records every session and pushes transcripts with your commits.
- Never paste secrets, tokens or `.env` contents into prompts or code.
- Do not disable Entire or remove its hooks.

## Commits
- The subject says what the product can now do: imperative, under ~60 characters.
- One logical change per commit.
- No AI attribution or co-author trailers. The `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added
  automatically and must stay.
- No em dashes.

**What's on `main`** (PRs #1 and #4)
- **`./hq` CLI:** commands to claim an issue, release it, open a PR, see the board, ship, check, set up a machine and bootstrap a repo. It's coordination only, works with any agent, and runs on Mac and Windows. Its unit tests pass on Python 3.9 and 3.14, and CI passes.
- **Agent rules:** `AGENTS.md` is the single rule file; Codex and Cursor read it directly and `CLAUDE.md` imports it for Claude Code. There are four skills: `hq-work`, `hq-plan`, `hq-review` and `hq-ship`.
- **Docs:** `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` for the two of you (kick-off, starting agents in each tool, onboarding your teammate). There's also a brief listing the prize tracks, and empty spec and architecture docs waiting for your context.
- **Entire:** session capture for all three agents, the Graph code map, the Brain memory, and a shared review profile with a Claude reviewer, a Codex reviewer and a Codex judge. Checkpoints go to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, the branch Entire's judging tool reads.
- **GitHub:** labels, milestones and squash-only merges that keep Entire's checkpoint links. `main` requires a PR, and a local hook blocks commits on `main`. The repo is marked as a template.

**Tested against the real repo**
- A blocked issue couldn't be claimed.
- Two agents claiming the same issue at once produced exactly one winner.
- `./hq pr` opened PR #4 with the issue's labels.
- The board flagged a file that two open PRs both changed.
- `./hq ship` merged PR #4, closed issue #2 and moved the issue waiting on it to ready.
- The merge commit on `main` kept all 8 of Entire's checkpoint links.
- The smoke-test issues, PR and branches are closed or deleted.

**Things to know**
- **Pushes:** the first push usually fails with `remote rejected (failed)` and the second goes through. Entire uploads checkpoints during every push. `./hq pr` retries on its own; for a manual push, just run it again.
- **Trails:** Entire opens a trail for every PR by itself, so the rules now tell agents to check for one rather than create one. My manual attempt made a duplicate, which I closed.

   ### Scope

# Architecture

Source of truth for layout, lanes and contracts. The full product brief is `docs/hack/kip-brief.md`.
Change a contract only through its own issue.

## Stack
One TypeScript API and one ingest worker in one Docker image on a Vultr instance in London, behind
Caddy (HTTPS via an `<ip>.sslip.io` hostname), provisioned by Terraform.

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| iOS app | Swift/SwiftUI, HealthKit, AVAudioRecorder metering, on-device voice-activity check, CoreLocation, background audio |
| API + worker | TypeScript, Hono, Zod, node-cron. Node 22, npm workspaces, `tsx` in dev, `esbuild` bundle for the image |
| Time series | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB): hypertables + a continuous aggregate for the 30-night average per sensor |
| Documents | MongoDB Atlas with 2dsphere indexes: users, night summaries, hotels, sensors, permits, venues, scores |
| AI | Gemini API (paid-tier key): clip labels, morning briefing, complaint draft, JSON output |
| Voice | ElevenLabs: TTS briefing, Scribe second-opinion classifier, Sound Effects for the demo clip |
| Chain | Solana mainnet, Memo program only (no Anchor) |
| Dashboard | React, Vite, MapLibre GL with OpenStreetMap tiles, served by the API |
| Infra | Terraform: Vultr instance, firewall, container registry; MongoDB Atlas IP access list |

`./hq check` runs `npm run -s typecheck` and `npm test --silent` across all workspaces (set by the
skeleton issue). `./hq setup` runs `npm install`.

## Repo layout

```
apps/api/                Hono API: /api routes, Street Manager SNS endpoint, live SSE, serves the dashboard
apps/worker/             node-cron ingest worker: Observatory every 5 min, OpenStreetMap daily
apps/web/                React + Vite + MapLibre dashboard, one folder per feature
apps/ios/                Xcode project (Mac + Xcode only, not buildable by cloud agents)
packages/shared/         CONTRACTS: Zod schemas, TS types, JSON fixtures for every payload
packages/scoring/        pure logic, no I/O: WHO curve, Lnight, attribution, construction hours, Quiet Stay Score
packages/tiger/          TimescaleDB migrations + typed client
packages/mongo/          MongoDB collections, indexes, repositories, aggregation pipelines
packages/gemini/         Gemini client: clip labels, briefing, complaint draft
packages/elevenlabs/     ElevenLabs client: TTS, Scribe, Sound Effects
packages/solana/         night-log hashing + Memo write/verify
infra/terraform/         Terraform + cloud-init template
data/samples/            recorded fixtures (Observatory, Street Manager, OSM, cohort)
scripts/                 one-off scripts (backfill, seed, demo assets)
assets/demo/             demo audio clips
docs/data/               notes on each external data source
Dockerfile               one image, runs api or worker
```

## Monorepo rules (they stop parallel agents colliding)
- **Internal imports use path aliases, not package deps.** `tsconfig.base.json` maps `@kip/<name>` to
  `packages/<name>/src/index.ts`. Never add an internal package to another `package.json`.
- **Each package owns its `package.json`.** Add external deps only to the workspace you are working
  in, with exact versions (`npm install --save-exact -w <workspace> <dep>`). The root
  `package.json` belongs to the skeleton issue: do not edit it in feature issues.
- **No lockfile is committed** (`package-lock.json` is gitignored), so parallel PRs never conflict on
  it. Exact versions keep installs reproducible.
- **Route and job stubs exist from day one.** The skeleton creates one stub file per API route and per
  worker job and mounts them all. A feature issue replaces only its own stub file.
- **Dashboard features live in `apps/web/src/features/<feature>/`.** The scaffold creates a
  placeholder `index.tsx` for each feature and the app shell; feature issues edit only their folder.
- **Every payload has a fixture** in `packages/shared/fixtures/`. Build UI and API code against the
  fixtures first, so you never wait for another lane's live data.
- **Secrets stay out of code and prompts.** Read them from env vars; tests mock every external call.

## Lanes

| Lane | Dirs | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| contracts | `packages/shared` | Ellis (the iOS owner signs off on the upload schema) |
| api | `apps/api` | Ellis |
| ingest | `apps/worker`, `data/samples`, `docs/data`, `scripts/` (ingest and seed scripts) | Ellis |
| web | `apps/web` | Ellis |
| scoring | `packages/scoring` | Ellis |
| db | `packages/tiger`, `packages/mongo` | Ellis |
| integrations | `packages/gemini`, `packages/elevenlabs`, `packages/solana` | Ellis |
| infra | root config, `Dockerfile`, `infra/`, `.github/` | Ellis |
| ios | `apps/ios` | Teammate |
| demo | `docs/demo`, `assets/demo`, `scripts/demo` | Both |

## Contracts

| Contract | Lives in | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NightUpload`: what the phone sends after a night | `packages/shared/src/night.ts` | Swift mirrors it as `Codable` in `apps/ios`. Agree it first: both tracks build on it |
| `NightSummary`, `Timeline`: what the API returns for a night | `packages/shared/src/night.ts` | One Mongo document per night |
| `SensorLevel`: city map payload | `packages/shared/src/sensors.ts` | `lnight30`, `pctHighlySleepDisturbed`, `indicative: true` |
| `HotelScore`, `Profile`: Quiet Stays payload | `packages/shared/src/hotels.ts` | Score 0 to 100 with components and sources |
| `LiveEvent`: phone to dashboard stream | `packages/shared/src/live.ts` | SSE payload |
| `ClipLabel`, `Briefing`, `EvidenceReport`, `Permit` | `packages/shared/src/*.ts` | |

Conventions: camelCase fields, timestamps as ISO-8601 UTC strings, noise as relative dB (the phone
mic is not calibrated), coordinates as `{ lat, lon }`, GeoJSON only inside MongoDB.

## API surface (stub files created by the skeleton)

| Route | File |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | `apps/api/src/app.ts` |
| `POST /api/nights`, `GET /api/nights/:id` | `apps/api/src/routes/nights.ts` |
| `POST /api/clips` | `apps/api/src/routes/clips.ts` |
| `GET /api/nights/:id/briefing`, `GET /api/audio/:id` | `apps/api/src/routes/briefing.ts` |
| `GET /api/sensors` | `apps/api/src/routes/sensors.ts` |
| `GET /api/hotels` | `apps/api/src/routes/hotels.ts` |
| `POST /api/live/events`, `GET /api/live/stream` | `apps/api/src/routes/live.ts` |
| `POST /api/nights/:id/anchor`, `GET /api/nights/:id/evidence`, `GET /api/nights/:id/verify` | `apps/api/src/routes/evidence.ts` |
| `DELETE /api/users/:id` | `apps/api/src/routes/users.ts` |
| `POST /api/street-manager/sns` | `apps/api/src/routes/street-manager.ts` |

## Env vars
Secrets live in `.env`, never committed. `.env.example` lists them all. Conductor copies `.env*`
into each new workspace via `.worktreeinclude`. Cloud agents get no secrets: they build against
fixtures and mocks, and a human runs the `needs:keys` steps.

| Name | Used by | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | api | `$CONDUCTOR_PORT` locally, 8080 in the image |
| `MONGO_URI` | api, worker | MongoDB Atlas |
| `TIGER_URI` | api, worker | Tiger Cloud service |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL` | api | Google AI Studio, paid tier (required for UK-facing apps) |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID` | api, scripts | ElevenLabs |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL`, `SOLANA_SECRET_KEY` | api | a mainnet RPC and a funded keypair (tiny SOL) |
| `VULTR_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY` | terraform | Vultr, Atlas |
| `TF_VAR_admin_ip`, `TF_VAR_atlas_project_id`, `TF_VAR_mongo_uri`, `TF_VAR_tiger_uri` | terraform | your IP, Atlas, Tiger |

## Deploy
`terraform -chdir=infra/terraform apply` builds the stack; the image is pushed to the Vultr
registry and cloud-init runs the api and worker containers. Live demo of infra as code:
`terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api` rebuilds only the server. Ellis owns deploys. The demo
runs from tag `demo-v1`.

## Cloud agents
Cloud agents (Codex cloud, Cursor background agents, Claude Code on the web) usually cannot run
`gh`, `./hq` or Entire, and cannot build `apps/ios`. A human claims the issue for them
(`./hq claim N --agent <tool> --workspace cloud-<k>`) before dispatching. The agent's PR description
must contain `Closes #N`. Give cloud agents issues without the `needs:mac` label; `needs:keys` issues
can be coded in the cloud, but a human runs the keyed verify step.

input.description: Read the spec and domain docs

result.output:
# Spec

What we build. `/hq-plan` turns it into issues. Business detail is in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, the
science and wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Problem
The city measures night noise, but people feel it, and nobody connects the two. Newcastle's
Urban Observatory publishes kerbside noise levels and WHO publishes how night noise disturbs sleep,
yet a resident can't tell what woke them, and a traveller can't tell that a hotel overlooks a
24-hour demolition site. Bewick Court residents were kept awake until 5am by demolition under a
24-hour permit, and no open dataset recorded it.

## Product
Kip shows how the city's noise affects sleep, street by street, and turns that into a Quiet Stay
Score for every hotel in Newcastle. It has three layers:

| Layer | Feature | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| City | City sleep map | Each Observatory noise sensor shaded by an indicative % of nearby residents highly sleep disturbed |
| Personal | Personal night | Timeline of sleep stages, bedroom noise and wake-ups, each tagged with its likely cause |
| Personal | Morning briefing | Spoken summary on Watch or AirPods: "Two wake-ups followed drilling at 06:41, before the 8am limit" |
| Personal | Evidence log | An out-of-hours noise report for the council, its hash anchored on Solana |
| Business | Quiet Stays | Hotels ranked by predicted sleep quality for the traveller's profile, with booking links |

City map and Personal night are the core; the rest build on them.

## Users
- **Resident** near construction or nightlife: wants to know what wakes them and whether it broke
  the council's construction hours, with evidence they can send.
- **Traveller** choosing a Newcastle hotel: wants to know where they will sleep well, weighted for
  how they travel (light sleeper, night out, best value, business).
- **Judges**: see real city data, a real recorded night and one live noise event.

## Demo script (3 min)
One live moment carries the pitch: a drilling sound hits the phone, and Kip labels it, checks the
council's hours and briefs you within seconds.

| # | Time | Step | P |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0:00 | Hook: Bewick Court. "Where in Newcastle would you sleep worst tonight? Nobody can tell you. Kip can." | P0 |
| 2 | 0:20 | City map: real Observatory data, sensors shaded by an indicative 30-night estimate of residents highly sleep disturbed | P0 |
| 3 | 0:50 | Live noise event: phone on the table in demo mode (no Watch data). ElevenLabs-generated drilling clip played from a speaker held against it. Dashboard shows the spike, Gemini labels it "construction", Kip flags it as outside council hours, the ElevenLabs briefing plays | P0 |
| 4 | 1:40 | A real night recorded at home: sleep stages, bedroom noise, wake-ups, shown as counts against the random baseline | P0 |
| 5 | 2:10 | Quiet Stays: switch profile "Light sleeper" to "Night out", ranking reorders; a hotel penalised for works on the stay dates | P0 |
| 6 | 2:35 | Trust: edit a log, show it no longer matches its Solana memo. Flash `terraform plan` and the Entire session record | P1 |
| 7 | 2:50 | Business: affiliate commission now, Verified Quiet next, data licensing later | P0 (slide) |

If a P1 step isn't working at the freeze, cut it from the script rather than slip.

## MVP scope (M1)
- Kip app on iOS (Expo): relative dB logged once a second, a 10-second clip around each spike,
  on-device check that drops clips with speech, recording while locked, HealthKit read of the
  Watch's sleep stages, heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate after the night ends, upload to the
  API, and a live demo mode that streams dB.
- Ingest worker: Observatory noise, NO2 and PM2.5 every 5 minutes, plus a backfill of at least
  30 nights; OpenStreetMap hotels and venues.
- API: night upload, clip labelling (Gemini, then delete the clip), wake-up attribution,
  construction-hours check, briefing text (Gemini) and voice (ElevenLabs), city map data, hotel
  ranking per profile, Street Manager SNS endpoint (or a recorded sample).
- Kip app on web (same Expo codebase, the demo dashboard): city map, night timeline, live event
  view, Quiet Stays page.
- Deployed on Vultr via Terraform, HTTPS via Caddy on an sslip.io hostname.

## Non-goals
- Calibrated dB from the phone. Kip uses spikes relative to the night's own baseline.
- Room-level hotel scores. The score describes a hotel's surroundings.
- Claiming noise *caused* a wake-up. Kip shows a link.
- Real affiliate bookings. Demo links are placeholders.
- Building or demolition sites outside Street Manager, except as heard by the bedroom microphone.
- An all-night Watch workout session (drains 40% to 100% of the battery). Read HealthKit instead.

## Stretch (M2, in priority order)
1. Solana Memo anchoring and the tamper demo (P1).
2. ElevenLabs Scribe as a second noise classifier; disagreements become "uncertain" (P1).
3. Complaint draft for the council from the evidence log (P1).
4. Simulated user cohort on the map and in hotel scores, labelled as simulated (P1).
5. Native watchOS target: haptics, "something woke me" button, briefing playback. Only if Watch signing
   works in the first 2 hours (P2).
6. Air quality factor in the hotel score (P2).

## Open questions
These change the plan. Until answered, the assumption in brackets holds.
- Does one of us sleep at home in Newcastle during the event, near an Observatory noise sensor?
  Demo step 4 depends on it. [Yes; otherwise the city map uses sensors near the venue and step 4
  uses a night exported from HealthKit.]
- How long is the event, and when does it start? [24 hours from about 10am.]
- Is each team limited to one sponsor track? [No. If yes, enter MongoDB: see
  `docs/DECISIONS.md`.]
- What does the "35" in the team's notes mean: a dB threshold, or a 35 m radius around a site?
  [Unknown; don't build on it.]
=================== DOMAIN
# Domain

The science, rules and wording Kip depends on. Code that computes, labels or displays any of
these must follow this file. Constants live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, not inline.

## Night noise and the WHO curve
- **Night window:** 23:00 to 07:00, `Europe/London` local time (handle BST changes).
- **Lnight:** the A-weighted equivalent level over the night window. It is an *energy* average,
  not an arithmetic mean of dB:
  `Lnight = 10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`.
  In Tiger, average `power(10, db / 10)` and convert back with `10 * log10(...)`.
- **City estimate:** per sensor, the energy average of nightly Lnight over at least the last 30
  nights. Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor as "not enough data", don't shade it.
- **WHO road-traffic curve** (Basner & McGuire 2018), % highly sleep disturbed:
  `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * Lnight + 0.0126 * Lnight^2`.
  This reproduces the plan's figures (2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB). Still check
  the paper before quoting more decimals.
- **Valid range:** 40 to 65 dB Lnight. Outside it, clamp for shading and mark the value as
  out of range; never extrapolate.
- **Thresholds** (WHO 2018): night-time road traffic below 45 dB Lnight, rail 44 dB, aircraft
  40 dB.
- **Limits:** the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's most exposed facade.
  Observatory sensors sit at the kerb and also pick up nightlife and voices. So the map is an
  *indicative road-traffic estimate*, never a measured disturbance rate.

## Bedroom noise (phone)
- The iPhone microphone is not calibrated. Store and show **relative dB** only.
- Sample once a second. A **spike** is a level above the night's own baseline (rolling median)
  by a threshold set in `packages/shared`. Keep a 10-second clip around each spike.
- On-device voice-activity check: any clip containing speech is dropped on the phone and never
  uploaded.

## Wake-up attribution
- **Wake-up signals:** a Watch "awake" stage during the sleep session, or a sudden heart-rate
  jump during sleep (Watch stages are coarse and miss brief arousals).
- **Method:** look for a spike in the 60 to 120 seconds before each wake-up, and compare the hit
  rate against randomly chosen windows of the same length from the same night.
- **Small numbers:** one night has 2 to 6 wake-ups. Show counts ("3 of 4 wake-ups followed a
  spike"). Show a percentage only once several nights are pooled from HealthKit history.
- HealthKit sleep stages appear only after the sleep session ends. Live demo mode needs no Watch
  data.

## Noise classification
- Labels: `construction`, `traffic`, `siren`, `snoring`, `other`, plus `uncertain`.
- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
  give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
  snoring being blamed on the building site.
- The clip is deleted once labelled. Only the label is kept.

## Construction hours (Newcastle City Council)
Recommended hours for noisy construction work:

| Day | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Monday to Friday | 08:00 to 18:00 |
| Saturday | 08:00 to 13:00 |
| Sunday and bank holidays | None |

A `construction` event outside these hours is flagged "outside council hours". Bank holidays for
England come from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` (`england-and-wales`). These are
*recommended* hours: say "outside the council's recommended hours", not "illegal".

## Street Manager
DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits in England (location, work category,
traffic management type, proposed and actual times) over AWS SNS to a public HTTPS endpoint. The
subscription must be confirmed within 3 days. It covers roads, not building or demolition sites.
Night work is inferred from proposed times and traffic management type.

## Evidence log and Solana
Each night's log is serialised canonically, hashed (SHA-256), and the hash written to Solana
mainnet with the Memo program (no Anchor). It proves *when* a log existed, not that its contents
are true. Never claim more.

## Wording rules
Anything user-facing, in the briefing prompt, the app (iOS or web) or the pitch:

| Say | Never say |
|---|---|
| "linked to", "followed" | "caused by" |
| "indicative estimate" | "measured disturbance", "% of residents are disturbed" |
| "outside the council's recommended hours" | "illegal", "breach" |
| "relative dB" for phone data | bare "dB" for phone data |
| "simulated" on cohort data | anything implying simulated users are real |
| "proves when the log existed" | "proves the noise happened" |

## Privacy (UK GDPR)
Sleep and heart data are special-category health data.
- Explicit, separate consent per data type: microphone, HealthKit, location.
- Store only relative dB, labelled events and HealthKit summaries. No raw audio at rest.
- Audio clips are deleted once labelled; clips with speech never leave the phone.
- One action deletes everything a user has, in both databases.
- Never log raw health values or audio in server logs.

# Decisions

Append-only log, newest at the bottom. Add an entry when a choice would surprise a newcomer or is
costly to undo. Agents also record it with `entire brain remember "<decision>"`.

Format:

```
## YYYY-MM-DD: <decision>
**Context:** why it came up.
**Decision:** what we chose.
**Consequences:** what follows, good and bad.
```

## 2026-11-13: GitHub Issues is the single task queue
**Context:** Up to ~10 agents across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor need one shared view of the
work. A second tracker (beads, Backlog.md, Task Master) would drift from GitHub.
**Decision:** Every task is a GitHub issue in the task form. `./hq` claims, labels and ships them.
Humans dispatch; agents never pick their own.
**Consequences:** GitHub is the only shared state; `.context/` and workspaces are scratch. Every
agent needs `gh` auth and network access.

## 2026-11-13: Entire for sessions, memory and review
**Context:** We want shared session history, codebase mapping, persistent memory and cross-vendor
review, and we target Best Use of Entire. Entire's judging tool only reads `refs/heads/entire/*`.
**Decision:** Use Entire Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails, and `entire review` (Claude Code and
Codex reviewers, one judge). Use the `branch` checkpoint backend.
**Consequences:** Every session is recorded and pushed, so no secrets in prompts. Each clone runs
`entire enable`. `review:pass` needs local `entire review`, hosted Trail review or `/hq-review`.

## 2026-11-13: Squash merges keep Entire-Checkpoint trailers
**Context:** Entire links commits to sessions through `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. A squash
message without them breaks the link.
**Decision:** Squash merge only. Repo setting: squash title = PR title, message = commit details.
`./hq ship` merges this way.
**Consequences:** `main` gets one commit per PR and `entire why` still resolves to sessions. Never
edit the trailers out of a squash message.

## 2026-11-13: Fresh submission repo from this template at kick-off
**Context:** MLH only judges work done during the event, and Entire's judging tool scores a clean
start higher.
**Decision:** This repo is a template. At kick-off we run `gh repo create --template` and hack in
the new repo.
**Consequences:** The submission has no pre-event history. Pre-kick-off agent sessions are closed
and fresh ones started. The README discloses the framework as pre-event tooling.

## 2026-11-14: Kip is the project
**Context:** The plan "Kip: Sleep, Noise and the City" (Nick, 2026-11-14) covers product, business
model, stack, build plan and pitch.
**Decision:** Build Kip. Product in `docs/SPEC.md`, business in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, science and
wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`, stack and contracts in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
**Consequences:** Every agent follows `docs/DOMAIN.md` for anything it computes or shows.

## 2026-11-14: The API is the only caller of third-party services
**Context:** Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana need secret keys; the app (iOS and web) is a client.
**Decision:** Only the API calls Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana. Clients call the API.
**Consequences:** Keys live in one place. Clip labelling and briefings need a network round trip.

## 2026-11-14: Tiger for time series, MongoDB for documents and geo
**Context:** Kip has dense timestamped data (1 Hz noise, sensor readings, vitals) and geo
documents (hotels, sensors, works). Both are sponsor tracks.
**Decision:** Every timestamped value goes in Tiger; MongoDB holds users, one summary per night,
hotels, sensors, works, venues and scores. If the event limits us to one sponsor track, enter
MongoDB: move the time series into MongoDB time series collections and make hotel ranking the
centrepiece.
**Consequences:** Two stores to provision and delete from. User deletion must cover both.

## 2026-11-14: Read Watch data through HealthKit, not a Watch app
**Context:** An all-night workout session drains 40% to 100% of a Watch battery, and Watch app
signing is a known time sink.
**Decision:** The iPhone reads the Watch's own sleep tracking from HealthKit after the night ends.
A watchOS app is a stretch, abandoned if signing doesn't work by hour 2.
**Consequences:** Sleep stages arrive only after the session ends, so the live demo uses the
phone alone.

## 2026-11-14: Claim links, not causes; label estimates
**Context:** One night has 2 to 6 wake-ups, phone dB is uncalibrated, and the WHO curve is for
long-term road traffic at the facade, not kerbside sensors.
**Decision:** Show counts against a random-window baseline, relative dB, and an "indicative" city
map. Follow the wording table in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.
**Consequences:** Weaker-sounding claims that survive judge questions.

## 2026-11-14: Placeholder booking links for the demo
**Context:** Affiliate approval takes weeks; Booking.com cut small affiliates in 2025.
**Decision:** Hotels come from OpenStreetMap with placeholder booking links. Apply to a network
anyway and don't quote a commission rate until confirmed.
**Consequences:** Revenue is shown as the model, not as live bookings.

## 2026-11-14: Solana mainnet with the Memo program only
**Context:** We want cheap public timestamps a council can check without trusting Kip.
**Decision:** Hash each night's log and write it to mainnet with the Memo program. No Anchor, no
custom program.
**Consequences:** No toolchain setup; a fraction of a penny per night. It proves when a log
existed, not that it's true, and we say so.

## 2026-11-14: Bun workspaces; one server package and image
**Context:** The API and worker share clients, schemas and database code, and the plan wants one
Docker image.
**Decision:** Bun is the package manager for the whole repo and the server runtime.
`apps/server` holds both entrypoints (`main.api.ts`, `main.worker.ts`) and builds with the Expo
web export into one image.
**Consequences:** One build and deploy, one lockfile. Never hand-merge `bun.lock`.

## 2026-11-14: React Native on Expo for both the phone and the dashboard
**Context:** The team's strongest language is TypeScript, and the demo needs an iPhone app and a
browser dashboard.
**Decision:** One Expo app (dev client, Expo Router) builds iOS and web. HealthKit through
`@kingstinct/react-native-healthkit`; background metering, spike clips and the speech check in a
small local Expo Module (`kip-audio`, Swift). Replaces the plan's SwiftUI app and React/Vite
dashboard.
**Consequences:** One UI codebase and shared types. The native audio module is the riskiest
piece: build and test it on a device first. Maps need a `.native`/`.web` split. A watchOS app
becomes a separate native target, so it stays a stretch.

## 2026-11-14: tRPC on Hono for the API
**Context:** App and server are both TypeScript, and several agents change API shapes in parallel.
**Decision:** tRPC v11 mounted on Hono. Every JSON call and the live subscription go through
tRPC; plain Hono routes only for binary clip upload, the Street Manager SNS endpoint, health and
the web build.
**Consequences:** End-to-end types with no codegen; a server change that breaks the app fails
typecheck. Non-TypeScript clients (SNS) still get plain HTTP.

## 2026-11-14: File tree by feature, then by layer
**Context:** Up to ~10 agents work at once. A layer-first tree (`routes/`, `services/`,
`screens/`) puts every task in the same folders.
**Decision:** Each feature (`city`, `night`, `attribution`, `labels`, `briefing`, `evidence`,
`stays`, `works`, `live`, `account`) owns a folder in `apps/mobile/src/features/`,
`apps/server/src/features/` and `packages/shared/src/`. Lanes are features. Registries are
written once in M0 with every feature stubbed; shared code changes through `platform` issues.
**Consequences:** Parallel issues touch disjoint paths. Cross-feature calls go through a feature's
`index.ts`. The rules are in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## 2026-11-14: Both of us own everything
**Context:** The template gave Ellis `main`, deploys and the freeze, and gave each human lanes.
With two people working across the whole stack, that split only adds hand-offs.
**Decision:** No split ownership. Either of us can merge any PR, deploy, call the freeze and tag
`demo-v1`. Lanes stay, but only to keep parallel agents on disjoint paths.
**Consequences:** No waiting on a specific person. Say in chat before merging contracts, deploy
config or anything after the freeze, so we don't both do it.

# Business

How Kip makes money and what the Quiet Stay Score is. Read this for any work on hotels, scoring,
profiles or booking links. Scoring maths and wording rules are in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Model
Kip recommends hotels on how well you'll sleep there and what's around them, and takes affiliate
commission on each booking. The same data that powers the city map and the personal night powers
the hotel ranking, so the business layer costs little extra to build.

## Quiet Stay Score (0 to 100)
One score per hotel, built from data Kip already collects. It describes the hotel's surroundings,
not a specific room: the side of the building and the floor can matter as much as the street.

| Input | Source | Effect on score |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative night-noise disturbance | Nearest Observatory noise sensors, distance-weighted, 30-night Lnight through the WHO road-traffic curve | Main factor |
| Active roadworks within 200 m | Street Manager permits; work scheduled at night (from proposed times and traffic management type) weighs more | Penalty for the dates of the stay only |
| Air quality at night | Observatory NO2 and PM2.5 | Small factor |
| Real nights nearby | Opted-in Kip users sleeping within 300 m | Corrects the estimate once there's enough data |
| Distance to nightlife and sights | OpenStreetMap venues | A preference, not a penalty (see profiles) |

### Profiles
Kip asks one question up front and re-weights the score.

| Profile | What Kip ranks first |
|---|---|
| Light sleeper | Lowest predicted disturbance |
| Night out | Within walking distance of nightlife, then quietest |
| Best value | Most quiet points per pound per night |
| Business | Quiet on weeknights, close to the station |

### Rules for the score
- It is an estimate and the UI says so. Every score has its sources one tap away: which sensors,
  which permits, how many real nights. Without this, low-scoring hotels will dispute it.
- Weights live in one place, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, so the app can show the breakdown.
- Simulated cohort nights are flagged and labelled wherever they affect a score.

## Revenue
1. **Affiliate commission (launch).** Booking links through affiliate networks. Booking.com cut
   thousands of smaller affiliates in 2025 and moved them to networks such as Awin and CJ;
   Expedia Group's affiliate programme and aggregators such as Travelpayouts are the other routes
   for a small team. Affiliate approval takes weeks, so the demo uses OpenStreetMap hotels with
   placeholder booking links. Don't quote a commission rate until it's confirmed.
2. **Verified Quiet (year one).** Hotels that already score well pay a yearly fee to replace the
   estimate with measured, room-by-room data from in-room sensors. Hotels that score badly get a
   free report showing which rooms and hours are the problem, as the route to a better score.
3. **Data licensing (later).** Area-level sleep disturbance data for councils, developers
   scheduling construction, and estate agents.

## Hypotheses, not findings
- Renters choosing a flat for a 12-month lease may be a bigger market than hotel guests: same
  score, higher stakes. Pitch it as the next market, not as evidence.

## Judge questions
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is this real data? | The city map, the recorded night and the permits are real; other users are simulated and labelled on the map |
| Does noise cause the wake-ups? | We claim a link, not a cause: wake-ups follow spikes more often than random moments do, shown as counts until there are enough nights for a percentage |
| Can you use the WHO curve on kerbside sensors? | Only as an indication: the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise, so we average 30 nights and label the map indicative |
| How accurate is a phone microphone? | Not calibrated, so Kip uses spikes above the night's own baseline in relative dB. The city estimate uses Observatory sensors, which were validated against precision meters |
| Do you record people's bedrooms? | Clips with speech are dropped on the phone; other clips are deleted once labelled. Health data needs explicit consent under UK GDPR, and users can delete everything |
| Why Solana? | Cheap public timestamps on mainnet that a council can check without trusting Kip. They prove when a log existed, not that it's true |
| Why two databases? | Timestamped numbers in Tiger, documents and geo queries in MongoDB |
| Why would hotels pay? | Well-scoring hotels pay to swap the estimate for measured, room-level data; low scorers get a free report on what to fix |

## Sponsor mapping
All seven sponsors do real work in Kip. The prize table with targets is in `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`.

| Sponsor | Role in Kip | What to show the judges | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vultr | Compute, Container Registry and firewall, all provisioned by Terraform | `terraform plan`, then `terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api` rebuilding the server while the data stays put | Strong |
| MongoDB Atlas | Users, night summaries, hotels and scores; geo queries | The hotel ranking pipeline: `$geoNear` on hotels, then `$geoWithin` lookups for nearby sensors and works | Strong |
| Gemini | Labels noise clips, writes the briefing and complaint draft, on a paid-tier key | Play a drilling clip and a siren clip; show the two labels | Strong |
| Tiger Data | All time-series data and the 30-night Lnight per sensor | The continuous aggregate that turns raw readings into the city map | Strong |
| ElevenLabs | Briefing voice, Scribe as a second classifier, Sound Effects for the demo clip | The briefing playing on AirPods, and the two classifiers agreeing | Medium to strong |
| Solana | Writes each night's log hash to mainnet with the Memo program | Edit a log on stage, re-hash it, show it no longer matches the on-chain memo | Medium |
| Entire | Records every agent session | One slide showing the recorded reasoning behind a key commit | Free win |

=================== anti-slop
---
name: anti-slop
description: Rejects glassmorphism, rainbow CTAs, cartoon empty states, and SaaS visual clutter. Use when reviewing AI-generated UI, polishing visuals, or removing decorative noise.
title: Anti Slop
category: visual-taste
severity: hard-rule
references:
- reference/slop-checklist.md
---

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- build and create
def check():
    keys = [i["key"] for i in I]
    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys)), "duplicate keys"
    lanes = set(json.load(open("hq.json"))["lanes"])
    for i in I:
        assert i["lane"] in lanes, (i["key"], i["lane"])
        for b in i["blocked"]:
            assert b in keys, (i["key"], "unknown blocker", b)
    order, seen, temp = [], set(), set()

    def visit(k):
        if k in seen:
            return
        assert k not in temp, "cycle at " + k
        temp.add(k)
        for b in by[k]["blocked"]:
            visit(b)
        temp.discard(k); seen.add(k); order.append(by[k])

    by = {i["key"]: i for i in I}
    for i in I:
        visit(i["key"])
    return order


def body(i, num):
    bl = ", ".join("#%d" % num[b] for b in i["blocked"]) or "none"
    notes = []
    if i["human"]:
        notes.append("Human task: not for agents.")
    else:
        envs = i["needs"] or ["cloud"]
        notes.extend(ENV[e] for e in envs)
    if i["read"]:
        notes.append("Read first: " + "; ".join("`%s`" % r for r in i["read"]) + ".")
    if i["notes"]:
        notes.append(i["notes"])
    notes.append("Parallel safety: stay inside Scope. Shared code changes go through their own `platform` issue "
                 "(`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, Rules that keep parallel agents apart).")
    return "\n\n".join([
        "### Goal\n\n" + i["goal"],
        "### Acceptance criteria\n\n" + "\n".join("- [ ] " + a for a in i["ac"]),
        "### Scope\n\n" + "\n".join("- " + (s if "`" in s else "`%s`" % s.split(" (")[0] + (" (" + s.split(" (", 1)[1] if " (" in s else ""))
                                    for s in i["scope"]),
        "### Do not touch\n\n" + i["dnt"],
        "### Blocked by\n\n" + bl,
        "### Verify\n\n" + "\n".join("- " + v for v in i["verify"]),
        "### Notes\n\n" + "\n".join("- " + n for n in notes),
    ]) + "\n"


def main():
    order = check()
    print("issues:", len(order))
    num, rows = {}, []
    for i in order:
        status = "status:needs-human" if i["human"] else ("status:blocked" if i["blocked"] else "status:ready")
        labels = [status, i["p"], "size:" + i["size"], "type:" + i["typ"], "lane:" + i["lane"]] + ["needs:" + n for n in i["needs"]]
        if DRY:
            num[i["key"]] = 100 + len(num)
            b = body(i, num)
            continue
        b = body(i, num)
        path = ".context/issues/%s.md" % i["key"]
        open(path, "w").write(b)
        cmd = ["gh", "issue", "create", "--title", i["title"], "--body-file", path, "--milestone", i["ms"]]

content.text:
Done. There are **74 issues (#8 to #81)** on GitHub, built on your `ARCHITECTURE.md`: Expo plus tRPC, the feature lanes, and registries written once in M0. They don't follow the PDF's original SwiftUI/Vite stack. Sorry for not pulling `main` at first; my duplicate docs were thrown away.

**How they're structured**
- Every issue has the sections `./hq` reads: Goal, Acceptance criteria, Scope, Do not touch, Blocked by (real issue numbers), Verify and Notes. Scope stays inside one feature lane, following your rules for keeping parallel agents apart.
- Labels on each issue:
  - status, priority, size, type and `lane:*` (your 12 lanes plus a new `demo` lane)
  - **`needs:mac`** for iOS and native audio work, which cloud agents can't build
  - **`needs:keys`** where one Verify step needs real keys; the code and mocked tests run in the cloud
- Milestones: M0 has 24 issues (skeleton, contracts, domain maths, clients), M1 has 34 (demo path), M2 has 10 (Solana, Scribe, cohort, stretch) and M3 has 6 (pitch, Devpost, rehearsal).

**What to dispatch now**
1. **#10, the Bun workspace, goes first, to a local agent**, because it edits the CI workflow. Nearly everything else waits on it.
2. These are ready for cloud agents now: #26 Terraform, #76 pitch, #77 Devpost, #78 Entire evidence, #79 DEV post.
3. Two jobs for you two: **#8, the hour-one sign-ups and keys**, and #9, the four open questions. #8 matters now because Street Manager and Gemini billing take time.

**Once #10 merges**, about 20 issues open up at once, which is enough to keep 5+ agents busy:
- registries (#11) and the app shell (#12)
- **#28, the night upload schema**, which should be agreed in the first 30 minutes
- domain maths (#14 to #17) and the database clients (#18)
- the integration clients (#19 to #24)
- feature contracts with fixtures (#29 to #31), so the screens and servers for city, live and stays can be built in parallel

**Dispatching a cloud agent**
1. Claim the issue for it with `./hq claim N --agent codex --workspace cloud-1`.
2. Send it the issue URL with "work on #N following AGENTS.md".
3. Its PR must start with `Closes #N`.

These rules are now in `AGENTS.md` and the playbook (PR #82, merged). The current state is on `./hq board`.
